decisions.reason: The footer remains shared across webpages; changing its owned background color does not alter the candidate's cross-page sharing or dark-theme rules.
The footer color preference does not change which legal documents are linked, their PDF format, or their browser-tab behavior.
The source changes the website footer's color but does not require the optional footer on the Provisioning Wizard or change the wizard's own background treatment.
The approved purple treatment concerns the footer, not the landing-page hero background or broader landing-page visual attributes.
The source preference concerns the website footer and does not establish a purple treatment for the distinct Console shell footer or other shell elements.
The footer background color does not affect the How It Works section's position, sequential presentation, or content.
A footer color change does not modify the reusable breakpoint or responsive-layout guidance.
The source does not require a footer on the Sign In page or change its Cognito customization, branding, background, or header-logo requirements.
The website footer color has no effect on the Console shell and application navigation-panel arrangement.
The same message merely observes that other consoles use monochrome buttons; it does not resolve the candidate's button-style ambiguity, and that observation is not an effect of the footer decision.
Approving the footer's purple background does not change the required design-system deliverables or resolve whether they belong in the brand guide.
The footer color preference does not change the plain-HTML, Tailwind CSS, or no-Astro implementation choices.
